clue.text: Charlie given sound suggestions on material

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: sound says the letters are written as the word is spoken, not as it is spelt

parts.note: suggestions are hints, a word whose ending is spoken with a buzzing Z sound

explanation.surface: Someone named Charlie offers spoken ideas about a piece of material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' and 'on' are link words. HINTS said out loud ends in a Z sound, so it is written HINTZ after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Chintz is a glazed printed cotton fabric, often floral, used for curtains and upholstery.

clue.text: Where one may land in Adelphi, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the place name might be rearranged into something else entirely

explanation.surface: A guide to landing somewhere in the Adelphi district, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Adelphi is an area of central London; 'in' is a link word and 'perhaps' asks for the letters of ADELPHI to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter touches down on a pad built for it, so that is a spot where a flyer can come down.

clue.text: Pays attention to composer's raw material

explanation.surface: Someone listens closely to what a composer starts from.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to observe it; and musical tones written on a stave are a composer's basic stuff.

clue.text: Semi-frozen, this thing gets hot at high point

indicators.note: semi means half, so only half of the word frozen is kept, here its back half

parts.note: this thing is a roundabout way of saying it
H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Something half-frozen warms up when it reaches its peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semi' keeps the last half of FROZEN, ZEN. 'gets' and 'at' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The zenith is the point in the sky directly overhead, hence a peak or culmination.

clue.text: Points to good person's home

parts.note: north and east are compass points, giving N and E
ST, for saint, is the crossword shorthand for a good person

explanation.surface: Directions leading to the house of someone virtuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'person's' carry the link: the saint's possessive just joins the definition on.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's nest is its home, and the word is used of any cosy dwelling.

clue.text: Novel left in South Wales

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A book abandoned somewhere in the south of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as a book but is the adjective meaning fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Newport is a city on the Usk estuary in south-east Wales, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: Slow mover sang avidly on and off

indicators.note: on and off says to take one letter, skip one, and so on through these words

explanation.surface: Something slow sang eagerly in fits and starts.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the first, third, fifth letters and so on of SANG AVIDLY gives S, N, A, I, L.
explanation.definitionFit: The snail is proverbially sluggish, crawling along on its single foot.

clue.text: Flipper's call to those in charge

explanation.surface: What a coin-tosser shouts out to the bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: The flipper is someone tossing a coin, who calls one side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-tosser calls the side bearing the monarch's face; and bosses are the people at the top of an organisation.

clue.text: Encounters beef or chicken in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation says the word is as spoken, so a soundalike spelling is wanted

parts.note: beef and chicken are kinds of meat, so together they are meats

explanation.surface: Someone comes across beef or chicken while chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet people is to come across them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Story about one returning to Israeli port

indicators.note: returning says the whole assembled piece is read backwards
about says the story goes round the numeral for one

parts.note: a story is a tale
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A tale about someone coming back to a port in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I into TALE, giving TALIE; 'returning' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eilat is Israel's harbour city on the Gulf of Aqaba at the Red Sea.

clue.text: Cinema movement with different current

parts.note: something different is new
a current is a flow in water, a wave

explanation.surface: A film trend with an alternative stream running through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word. The New Wave (nouvelle vague) was the French film movement of the late 1950s and 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Wave was a group of film-makers such as Godard and Truffaut who broke with studio convention.

clue.text: Initial payment is back in the garage

indicators.note: in says the turned-round word sits inside the garage word

parts.note: a depot is a garage for buses or vehicles

indicators.note: back says the little word is is read the other way round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A down payment is sitting at the rear of the car workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IS into SI, which goes 'in' DEPOT. 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is the first sum paid to secure a purchase, with the balance to follow.

clue.text: Little bird allowed painful cry first

indicators.note: first says the cry is placed in front of the word for allowed

parts.note: ow is what you shout when hurt
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A small bird was permitted to squawk in pain before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is called an owlet, so it is a small, baby bird.

clue.text: Regularly appearing on tendril, fly will enlighten

indicators.note: regularly says to take letters at even intervals, here every second one through these two words

explanation.surface: A fly perched on a plant tendril will teach you something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing on' and 'will' are link words. The second, fourth and so on letters of TENDRIL FLY are E, D, I, F, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct someone morally or intellectually, to improve their understanding.

clue.text: Burst of emotion having raised bottom of trousers?

parts.note: flares are trousers widening at the bottom, so a flare is that bottom part
raised means up

explanation.surface: A sudden outburst about a trouser hem being lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link word. The answer reads as a joke too: the bottom of the trousers is a flare, and lifted it is 'flare up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flare-up is a sudden outbreak of anger or another strong feeling.

clue.text: A last revision for map-book

indicators.note: revision means reworking, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: One final reworking of a book of maps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps.

clue.text: What people wear to shock, seen round about

indicators.note: seen round says the word for shock goes about the other piece

parts.note: to appal is to shock
re is Latin for concerning, about

explanation.surface: Clothing meant to startle, spotted somewhere close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word. 'shock' reads as the wearer's aim but just supplies a synonym; 'seen round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is clothing, the garments people put on.

clue.text: River fish when brought round for money

indicators.note: brought round says the fish is wrapped about the river letter

parts.note: luce is an old name for the pike
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A river fish caught and brought round for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' and 'for' are link words. LUCE (a pike) is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, especially gained dishonourably, as in 'filthy lucre'.

clue.text: Minister converts sprite

indicators.note: converts says the letters of sprite are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: A clergyman wins over a fairy to the faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' and 'converts' suggest religion; 'converts' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is a minister of religion, ordained to perform rites.

clue.text: Andrew perplexed without energy, looks tired

indicators.note: perplexed means muddled up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without says the energy letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Andrew, baffled and drained, appears worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes E from ANDREW, leaving ANDRW, which 'perplexed' rearranges. 'looks' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn face is haggard and strained from fatigue or worry.

clue.text: Excessive returning some smart luxury

indicators.note: returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some excessive smart luxury is coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks ARTLU out of smART LUxury; 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra as an adjective means going beyond the usual, extreme.

clue.text: Lavatory available to hire after I left!

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter I goes out of the word

parts.note: a lavatory is a toilet

explanation.surface: A loo becomes available for rent once I have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link word: once I has 'left' TOILET, the rest reads TO LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A property 'to let' is offered for rent, the sign on a vacant flat.

clue.text: Anyway, decorate again

indicators.note: anyway says the word reads the same whichever way you go

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whatever happens, do up the room once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyway' reads as 'regardless', but here it says the answer reads the same in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To put fresh wallpaper on a room is to redecorate it.

clue.text: A top spinning round one in courtyard

indicators.note: spinning round says the letters whirl into a new order, as a top does

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A spinning top goes round and round someone in the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. A, TOP and I are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor area next to a house, much like a small courtyard.

clue.text: Royal Engineers said to go free

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is written as it sounds, not as it is spelt

parts.note: to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Army engineers are told they can walk away at liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word. LEAVE spoken sounds like the second half of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of a burden is to free them from it.

clue.text: The unending argument of the cast

indicators.note: unending says the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: The endless quarrelling among the actors in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the' is a link. 'cast' reads as the actors but is the verb meaning hurl.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast a stone is to toss or hurl it.

clue.text: Bribe last of set in traveller's rest

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the word for bribe

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify or bribe

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word set

explanation.surface: Someone bribes the final member of a group at a roadside inn.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop is a halt on a journey, a pause where a traveller rests.

clue.text: Peep at empty licence to travel leisurely

parts.note: a peep is a short hoot of a horn, a toot

indicators.note: empty says the word licence loses its inside, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A glance at a blank driving permit before a gentle drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peep' looks like 'glance' but is the sound of a horn. 'at' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To tootle is to drive or wander along slowly and unhurriedly.
